metaDescription: Encrypt text with a password using AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2 in your browser. Free, output is base64, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Encrypt a piece of text with a password. The tool derives a key with PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations), encrypts with AES-256-GCM and gives you one base64 string.
why:
Sometimes you need to pass a short secret through a channel you do not trust: a note in a ticket, an email, a shared document. Encrypting it with a password first means the channel only ever sees ciphertext.

This tool uses the browser WebCrypto API, so there is no custom cryptography. A random salt and nonce are generated for every run, the key comes from your password through PBKDF2 with 600,000 iterations, and AES-GCM adds authentication so tampering is detected. The output is a single base64 string that carries a version byte, the iteration count, salt and nonce, ready for the matching decrypt tool. It is a convenience for short text, not a replacement for a vetted file encryption tool.
howTo: Enter the text to encrypt in the input box.
Type a strong password in the options. The default password is only a placeholder, so change it.
Run the tool to produce the base64 ciphertext.
Copy the output and share the password through a different channel.

faq.a: Base64 of a version byte, the iteration count, a 16-byte salt, a 12-byte IV and the ciphertext. Header bytes are authenticated. A fresh salt and IV are used each time, so the same input gives different output.

faq.q: Is it safe to use for important secrets?
faq.a: It uses standard primitives, but safety depends on your password. A weak password can be guessed offline. This is not audited software, so for high-stakes data use a reviewed tool.

faq.q: What if I forget the password?
faq.a: The text cannot be recovered. There is no reset and no copy on any server. Keep the password in a password manager.
No. Encryption runs in your browser through WebCrypto, and neither the text nor the password is sent anywhere. Closing the tab discards both from the page.
